events.title: Confederate Forces Fire on Fort Sumter
events.description: Confederate batteries under General P.G.T. Beauregard opened fire on the Union-held Fort Sumter in Charleston Harbor, South Carolina. After roughly 34 hours of bombardment, the fort's garrison under Major Robert Anderson surrendered on April 13.
events.significance: This event marked the beginning of the American Civil War, a conflict that would last four years, claim an estimated 620,000 or more lives, and end slavery in the United States.

events.title: Death of President Franklin D. Roosevelt
events.description: Franklin D. Roosevelt died of a cerebral hemorrhage at Warm Springs, Georgia, less than three months into his fourth term. Vice President Harry S. Truman was sworn in as the 33rd President that evening.
events.significance: Roosevelt had led the United States through the Great Depression and most of World War II. His death elevated Truman, who soon learned of the atomic bomb project and made the decision to use it, shaping the end of the war and the dawn of the nuclear age.

events.title: Polio Vaccine Declared Safe and Effective
events.description: On the tenth anniversary of Roosevelt's death, the University of Michigan announced that Dr. Jonas Salk's polio vaccine field trial had shown the vaccine to be safe and effective. The announcement led to the vaccine's immediate licensing in the United States.
events.significance: The vaccine began the path toward the near-elimination of polio, a disease that had paralyzed and killed thousands of children each year, and it stands as one of the great public health achievements of the 20th century.

events.title: Yuri Gagarin Becomes the First Human in Space
events.description: Soviet cosmonaut Yuri Gagarin launched aboard Vostok 1 from the Baikonur Cosmodrome and completed a single orbit of Earth in about 108 minutes before landing safely.
events.significance: Gagarin's flight was a milestone in human history and a major victory for the Soviet Union in the Space Race, intensifying competition with the United States and leading to President Kennedy's commitment to land a man on the Moon.

events.title: First Space Shuttle Launch
events.description: NASA launched Space Shuttle Columbia on mission STS-1 from Kennedy Space Center, crewed by John Young and Robert Crippen, exactly 20 years after Gagarin's flight. It was the first orbital flight of the reusable shuttle program.
events.significance: Columbia's maiden flight inaugurated the Space Shuttle era, demonstrating that a reusable winged spacecraft could launch into orbit and land like an aircraft, and it supported three decades of satellite deployment, scientific research, and construction of the International Space Station.
